newsitem.title: USA: Viacom, Sprint, set Internet pact.
newsitem.headline: Viacom, Sprint, set Internet pact.

text.p: Viacom Inc. and Sprint Corp. announced an agreement Monday to develop products to make it easier for consumers to find Viacom's products on the Internet.

Under the agreement, Sprint, the nation's third-largest long-distance carrier, will develop and distribute the products with Blockbuster Entertainment, Simon & Schuster, Macmillan Publishing and other companies owned by New York-based Viacom.
For Viacom, which also owns MTV, the pact could help spread its popular programmes and entertainment franchises to a new audience of Internet users.
Kansas City, Mo.-based Sprint started offering Internet services for consumers over the summer, joining its rivals AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp.
Sprint already provides Internet services to businesses and says it is the world's largest carrier of Internet traffic.

"Sprint has great expertise developing Internet applications for the commercial marketplace. This makes them a strong partner with which to develop unique products based on Viacom's array of brands," Edward Horowitz, Viacom's senior vice president for technology, said in a statement.
"Our relationship with Viacom marks an approach to the consumer marketplace that no other Internet Service Provider has taken," said Robba Benjamin, president of Sprint's multimedia group.
Viacom and Sprint expect to announce the first of the new product offerings later this fall.
Sprint stock rose 37.5 cents to $39.75 on the New York Stock Exchange and Viacom shares fell 37.5 cents to $35.375 on the American Stock Exchange.
